candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8: protect clients and healthcare personnel from health/environmental hazards; use equipment safely; follow safety plans and procedures.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — medical-device recall response
candidate.educational_objective: Respond to an FDA device recall by identifying affected equipment and implementing the recall-specific correction or removal instructions rather than assuming every recall requires destruction or continued use.

options.A: Identify affected devices and follow the recall-specific correction or removal instructions and facility policy.
options.B: Discard every recalled device permanently because every FDA recall requires removal and destruction.
options.C: Continue using every recalled device until it fails because recall notices are informational only.
options.D: Ignore the recall unless a patient has already been injured by the exact affected device in use.

candidate.rationale: FDA defines a medical-device recall as a correction or removal action used to address a problem with a device. A recall does not always require permanent removal or destruction; depending on the recall, the action may include inspection, adjustment, repair, relabeling, or another correction. The facility should therefore identify the affected devices and follow the recall-specific instructions and its internal recall process. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: When a device recall affects equipment in use, the facility should identify affected devices and follow the specific FDA/manufacturer correction or removal instructions; recall does not universally mean permanent destruction.
candidate.source_document_title: What Is a Medical Device Recall?
candidate.source_locator: FDA medical-device recall overview: a recall may involve correction or removal; a recall does not always mean a product must be stopped or returned and may require checking, adjusting, fixing, relabeling, or other correction.
candidate.source_version_date: Current FDA medical-device recall guidance; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
candidate.stem: A hospital receives an FDA medical-device recall notice for equipment currently in use. What is the most appropriate initial facility response?
